title: Littleton Med - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for onboarding Littleton Medical Group onto Redwood. Reviewed success criteria (latency < 150ms p95, HIPAA-like data controls, SSO + audit logs), deployment options (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC), initial pilot scope (appointments summarization + triage routing), and immediate next steps: share onboarding docs, schedule technical deep dive, provide sandbox credentials for pilot. Some audio/transcription glitches, a couple of product names misrecognized.

Deployment mode recommendation: Dedicated vs Private
Integration plan: SSO, webhook sinks, routing policies

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-08
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Littleton VP Product), Carlos Ruiz (Littleton DevOps), Leah Park (Littleton ML)

Summary:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan, account exec for Redwood. Quick intro from our side, Priya's our solutions engineer she'll run the tech bits.
[00:10] Maya: Hi, Maya here, thanks. We're excited to get started. Leah and Carlos are on the lin– on the call as well.
[00:15] Carlos: Hey all.
[00:20] Priya: Great, I'll go over the agenda briefly: success criteria, deployment options, pilot scope, and next steps. Then we can dive into networking/SSO questions.

[02:05] Jordan: For timeline, just to be explicit, Littleton wants a 4-week pilot, with a follow-up eval for production in early March, does that still sound right?
[02:15] Maya: Yep, 4 weeks is the goal. We need to validate latency p95 under 150ms for the routing use case and confirm we can meet our internal data security bar, which is aligned with HIPAA controls.

[04:00] Priya: On the deployment choices: for most teams doing pilots we recommend starting with Redwood Dedicated — predictable throughput and isolation — unless you need a fully private control plane. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and we can pin model versions. If you need VPC-level control and customer-managed networking we can look at Private (VPC) — that adds networking work but meets the strictest compliance.
[04:45] Leah: What are the differences in terms of operational overhead? If we go Dedicated, do we still need to orchestrate anything?
[04:55] Priya: Minimal from your side. Redwood manages the runtime, autoscaling policies, and kernel selection. For Dedicated you'll have a reserved pool; we offer configurable autoscaling and burst policies. For Private, you'll be more involved in networking and KMS integrations.

[06:30] Carlos: Latency wise, are we looking at p95 numbers that are region dependent? Our primary users are in the northeast.
[06:40] Priya: Yes region matters. Hosted is fastest to start but less isolated. Dedicated in an east region should meet your p95 target depending on sequence lengths and batching; we also provide batching and KV cache tuning. We'll run a benchmark with your sample traffic shape.

[09:10] Jordan: For success criteria, we'll note: p95 < 150ms, throughput of ~60 reqs/min initially, and demonstrable audit logs + SSO + RBAC for the pilot.
[09:30] Maya: Audit logs are non-negotiable. We need detailed request-level logs and retention options. Also we need keys managed by our KMS if possible.
[09:45] Priya: We support KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated — we can do key wrapping for tokens and customer-managed keys, and we capture request audit logs with per-token breakdown in the Console. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC 2 docs.

[12:00] Carlos: On networking, if we pick Dedicated, will we need to open inbound ports from our VPC to Redwood? How does the egress work?
[12:12] Priya: For Dedicated we typically do secure peering and encrypted tunnels. For Private we'd provision a VPC and you manage routing. We'll loop in our infra ops to map firewall rules. There may be one outbound endpoint for telemetry/metrics depending on the option.

[15:40] Leah: About the models: we want to run an appointments summarization model and a triage reranker. Can we pin versions and use quantized variants for cost?
[15:55] Priya: Yes, you can pin model versions and we have quantization profiles. For triage we sometimes recommend a smaller reranker model to avoid cost blowup. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization settings based on your workload.

[18:30] Jordan: A couple of typical tradeoffs to call out: bigger models reduce manual tuning but cost more; aggressive batching saves tokens but increases tail latency. We can tune autoscaling to prioritize p95 latency over unit cost for your SLA.

[20:00] Maya: We need SSO, SAML, and role-based access for the Console. Can you confirm SAML support and SCIM?
[20:10] Priya: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC with team roles, and audit trails. We'll send the SAML metadata example.

[22:50] Carlos: For data residency, our records say we must keep data in us-east. Is that a configuration?
[22:58] Priya: We can pin region routing and host inference in us-east for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted API we can prefer region but for guaranteed residency Dedicated/Private is recommended.

[26:00] Jordan: Let's talk about the pilot steps: 1) Redwood provides a Dedicated sandbox and credentials; 2) Littleton provides anonymized sample dataset and traffic shape; 3) Redwood will run a benchmark and share results; 4) we iterate on config (batching/KV cache/model variant); 5) produce pilot report.

[28:40] Maya: That sounds good. One ask — can you include a matrix of what features (KMS, audit retention, SSO) are available in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[28:50] Priya: Absolutely. We'll attach a matrix in the follow-up email.

[31:15] Leah: A technical note: for summarization we need streaming output to minimize UX latency. Any limitations?
[31:25] Priya: Streaming is supported. For streaming we still maintain KV cache semantics; we'll show expected throughput vs latency tradeoffs in the deep dive.

[34:05] Carlos: Are there any known gotchas with our internal kubernetes setup? We use private subnets and strict egress rules.
[34:15] Priya: For Private deployment that's fine; we'll provide a checklist. For Dedicated we'll need to open or peer to our endpoints; we'll send a firewall checklist. Expect some coordination with networking but nothing novel.

[37:00] Jordan: Pricing note: pilot can be done under a trial credit. For Dedicated there's a reserved commit if you go production, we'll outline options in the worksheet.
[37:30] Maya: Good to know. We also want clarity on the rollback/fallback policy if model degrades — auto-fallback to smaller model or previous version?
[37:40] Priya: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to pinned compatible variants; Redwood Console has controls for rollouts and automatic policy-based fallbacks.

[40:10] Jordan: Ok, we'll summarize and action items: Jordan send docs/pricing; Priya book the technical deep dive; Ops provision sandbox; customer to provide sample data and requirements. Anything else?
[40:25] Maya: Nope, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[40:30] Carlos: Thanks.
[40:33] Priya: Thank you — we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[40:40] Jordan: End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: there are a few misrecognized vendor names (VendorX) and some run-on sentences; otherwise most content captured.
